header.name: Task Priority Control of Robots
header.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to task-based control for robotic systems, equipping students with the knowledge and skills to design and implement advanced control strategies. The course explores the core concepts of defining and prioritizing robot tasks, focusing on the mathematical foundations of kinematics and inverse kinematics to enable precise robot behavior. The curriculum covers various control architectures for single and multi-robot systems, from kinematic to dynamic control layers, and examines real-world applications such as underwater manipulators, cooperative transportation, and human-robot interaction. By the end of the course, students will be able to formulate and prioritize control tasks, implement task-priority inverse kinematics algorithms, design robust control architectures, and analyze the performance of task-based control systems for diverse robotic challenges.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to explain the principles and advantages of task-based control for robotic systems

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to generate and prioritize control tasks for various robotic applications

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Design control architectures for single and multi-robot systems and analyze their performance

lecture_topics: Introduction to Task-Based Control: Concept of tasks and priorities in robot control
advantages of task-based control over traditional methods
applications in various robotic domains (e.g., industrial manipulators, mobile robots, humanoid robots)
Mathematical Foundations: Review of linear algebra and matrix operations
geometric and kinematic fundamentals of robots
transformation matrices, Jacobians, and null spaces
Task Specification and Prioritization: Defining tasks in terms of desired robot behavior
assigning priorities to tasks based on importance
handling equality and inequality constraints
Task-Priority Inverse Kinematics: Solving the inverse kinematics problem with task priorities
classic and modern task-priority algorithms
handling underactuated systems and redundancy
Control Architectures: Centralized vs. decentralized control for multi-robot systems
Kinematic and dynamic control layers
Integration of task-based control with mission planning
Applications and Case Studies: Underwater floating manipulator systems (UVMS)
Cooperative transportation and manipulation
Obstacle avoidance and navigation
Teleoperation and human-robot interaction
Advanced Topics: Optimization techniques for task-based control
Learning and adaptation in task-based frameworks
Challenges and future directions in task-based control
